meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (Republic of Panama; Registro Público de Panamá jurisdiction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic) with Delaware-model corporate law influence (hybrid corporate doctrine)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley General de Sociedades (Law 32 of 1927), as amended by Law 5 of 2015 and later reforms: Articles 1-10 (formation and capital), 15-17 (registry inscription), 25-27 (registered agent and office), together with the Panamanian Fiscal Code (Código Fiscal) for tax registration obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Personas Jurídicas y Asuntos Notables (Mercantile Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad Anónima (Public Deed of Incorporation) followed by the Certificado de Registro / Ficha Electrónica issued by the Registro Público.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement. The authorized capital is expressed in the public deed, but no escrow deposit is required by law. Shares may be subscribed at par or as issued shares, and payment may be deferred or made in kind. The registry does not require proof of bank deposit before incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED: 1. That the incorporators, having subscribed to the share capital of the Company, hereby ratify the issuance of shares to the initial shareholders. 2. That the board of directors adopts the registered office located at [City, Panama], as communicated to the Registro Público, and designates the registered agent. 3. That [Name] be and is hereby appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, or similar directors, with authority to execute banking, licensing, and tax filings. 4. That the officers are authorised to open corporate bank accounts, engage legal counsel, and complete all statutory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Nombre de Sociedades (online or in-person office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal name-reservation request via the Registro Público's e-portal or at the public registry window. Provide two proposed company names in order of preference. Pay the official search and reservation fee. The registrar verifies that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing entity. Upon approval, a name-reservation certificate is issued with a limited validity period.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form (Solicitud de Reserva de Nombre)
Photocopy of applicant passport or corporate identification
Payment receipt for the official fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a written reconsideration request or a new application with a distinct name. An administrative appeal may be lodged before the Dirección General of the Registro Público if the initial denial is contested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Circuit of Panama (Notaría Pública)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Panamanian attorney or notary to draft the Escritura Pública de Constitución. The deed must include the company name, capital structure, share classes, registered office, registered agent, directors and officers, and corporate purposes. The incorporators or their legal representatives must appear before the notary to execute the deed. The notary will authenticate the signatures and issue a certified original public deed.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of incorporation prepared by counsel
Passports or official ID of each incorporator
Power of attorney if a legal representative acts on behalf of an incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in the draft, correct the clauses and resubmit for notarization. If a power of attorney is insufficient, obtain a revised notarized power and execute the deed anew.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Corporation with the Registro Público
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Personas Jurídicas y Asuntos Notables
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Escritura Pública with the Registro Público, together with the cover sheet and payment of the statutory registration and stamp fees. The registry officer will examine the deed for legal compliance and, if accepted, issue the Ficha Electrónica (electronic corporate record) and the Certificate of Registration. This certificate proves the legal existence of the Sociedad Anónima.
required_dossiers: Original notarized Escritura Pública de Constitución
Copy of the name reservation approval
Official fee payment forms and receipts
Identification documents of directors and resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a 'glosa' (observation), the filer receives a written notice. Corrective amendments must be filed through a notarial rectification deed or supplementary document, and the file is resubmitted. If the glosa is contested, an appeal may be filed with the Registro Público's Director.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Obtaining the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Ficha Electrónica, apply for the RUC through the DGI's online platform or at the DGI office. Submit corporate documents and officer identification. The DGI issues the taxpayer identification number and the Aviso de Op (notice of taxable operations) form. This is required for opening bank accounts, invoicing, and declaring territorial-source income tax.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Registro / Ficha Electrónica issued by the Registro Público
Notarized copy of the Escritura Pública
Passport or ID of the legal representative
Proof of registered office address (lease, utilities statement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI queries the application, provide corrected or supplementary documentation via the DGI e-window. Re-file the RUC application after resolving the specific inconsistency, or file a formal administrative appeal if the denial is permanent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Licensing and Complementary Social Security Registration (If Applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá – Sección de Avisos de Operación; Caja de Seguro Social (CSS); Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For a purely digital stock-photography platform with no physical office, a municipal Aviso de Operación is generally not mandatory, but may still be issued if the company elects to maintain a local office. If employees are hired in Panama, register the company as an employer with CSS and MITRADEL. For remote or digital-only operations, this step is optional and can be deferred.
required_dossiers: If seeking municipal aviso: lease or title of the business premises
If hiring employees: employment contracts, officer ID, CSS registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality or CSS rejects the application, correct the declarations or provide proof of exemption for digital-only operations. Submit a written clarification to the head of the licensing section and, if required, file an appeal with the respective administrative tribunal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Empresas y Servicios
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required – the stock photography and generative media platform is a digital service without physical industrial operations. No vertical-sector operating permit is mandated under Panamanian law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAmbiente) – Dirección de Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Category 0) – the business comprises only digital administrative and office activities; no industrial process, infrastructure construction, or environmental discharge is involved.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. There are no wastewater discharges, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams associated with the virtual asset marketplace. If a small administrative office is operated, it must comply with general municipal sanitation and solid-waste disposal rules, but no specific environmental threshold applies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety certification, structural load inspection, or workplace clearance is required for a remote digital platform. If a physical office is later opened, it must obtain an inspection certificate from the Dirección General de Bomberos de Panamá (fire code compliance) and a basic workplace safety clearance from the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral, limited to standard office occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), República de Panamá; official portal https://www.dgi.gob.pa; e-filing via E-Tax 2.0/SITWEB; electronic invoice clearance via SIFE (Sistema de Facturación Electrónica).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Panama S.A. obtains its statutory tax identifier (RUC — Registro Único de Contribuyentes) in the following sequence: (1) incorporation by Panamanian notary and inscription in the Registro Público de Panamá; (2) appointment of a resident legal representative and of a registered agent (agente residente) establishing a valid tax domicile in Panama; (3) filing of the Aviso de Operación (commencement-of-operations notice) before the DGI through the E-Tax/SITWEB portal; (4) issuance by DGI of the definitive RUC certificate; (5) procurement of the qualified electronic signature/digital certificate required for SIFE e-invoicing; and (6) completion of the ITBMS registration module (empresario) where taxable supplies will be made in or from Panama. For a purely extraterritorial holding/export vehicle, the same steps in abridged form apply, but the entity must still maintain a Panama-based resident agent and an up-to-date RUC file.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No pass-through/check-the-box election exists for a Panama S.A.; the entity is taxable at entity level solely on Panama-source income and is not taxed on foreign-source income. The principal statutory elections available are: (i) selection of the simplified small-taxpayer regime (Régimen de Pequeños Contribuyentes) where annual gross revenue does not exceed B/. 36,000; (ii) admission to the Panama-Pacifico Special Economic Zone (Ley 41 de 2007) conferring income-tax, ITBMS and municipal-tax exemptions; (iii) the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime (Ley 41 de 2007) permitting 0% ITBMS on qualifying cross-border services; and (iv) hybrid-mismatch-driven elections in structuring the MNE chain such that foreign dividends, branch profits and capital gains sourced abroad remain outside Panamanian gross income under the territorial law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios), a VAT-type indirect tax; imports, internal transfers, and digital services are in scope, with separate customs duties under the Ley Aduanera.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 36,000 (Panamanian balboa at 1:1 parity with the U.S. dollar) of estimated annual gross turnover: taxpayers whose supplies will exceed this amount are required to operate as regular ITBMS taxpayers and issue authorized fiscal invoices; taxpayers at or below this level may use the simplified small-taxpayer regime. Non-resident digital service platforms supplying Panamanian consumers are subject to mandatory ITBMS collection/registration even without a physical presence when their Panamanian-sourced digital supplies exceed the statutory threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama operates a phased mandatory electronic invoicing mandate implemented through the DGI SIFE platform (Sistema de Facturación Electrónica de la DGI). Taxpayers transmit invoice data to DGI in XML/JSON through certified REST/SOAP API web services, obtain DGI authorization (digital stamp/sello digital) before invoice delivery in normal flow, and embed a validation QR code plus a qualified electronic signature on each e-invoice. Offline/contingency issuance is limited to a maximum of 24 hours, after which the invoice must be transmitted and sealed. Fiscal printers are accepted only for small taxpayers on a diminishing basis, and the DGI may suspend fiscal authorization where clearance APIs fail repeatedly.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and qualified offshore services are subject to ITBMS at the zero rate (0%). For goods, zero-rating requires the products to leave Panamanian customs territory and be covered by an accepted export customs declaration. For cross-border services — including stock-photo licensing and AI-generated visual-asset distribution — the zero rate applies only where the customer is a non-resident, the service is consumed and economically exploited abroad, the consideration is paid from abroad, and the income is remitted into the Panamanian banking system. Digital services that effectively benefit a Panamanian user cannot be zero-rated and remain within the standard 7% tax base.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Exportación / DUE) approved by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas
Bill of Lading (Conocimiento de Embarque) or Air Waybill evidencing physical exit of goods
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank certificate / SWIFT MT103 credit advice) demonstrating remittance of export proceeds in foreign currency into the Panamanian bank account
Commercial invoice and e-invoice bearing the 0% ITBMS export legend
Executed contract and customer certificate of non-residency for cross-border digital-asset services
Packing list, weight note, or electronic delivery log evidencing the foreign destination of the exported media/content
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating claims are scrutinized by DGI and customs through bank remittance matching, customs-exit verification, and foreign-beneficial-use testing for digital services. An unsubstantiated or simulated export triggers immediate reversal of the zero rating with clawback of the 7% ITBMS otherwise payable, recapture of input ITBMS credits previously deducted on export-related costs, a statutory recargo of 10% on the omitted tax, monthly interest of 1% or fraction thereof, and fines of 50%–150% of the evaded amount. The filing of false export declarations is a criminal tax offense under Ley 70 de 2019 (delitos tributarios), carrying imprisonment of 2–5 years, fines equal to one to two times the tax deficit, and personal civil liability of the directors and the resident agent; DGI may also suspend the taxpayer's RUC and SIFE authorization pending full repayment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco Nacional de Panamá (National Bank of Panama) as fiscal agent of the State; prudential and AML/CFT supervision is exercised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (Panama Banking Superintendency, SBP) under Decree-Law No. 3 of 1985, as amended. Panama has no traditional central bank, no foreign-exchange administration, and no monetary or FX policy authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is fully dollarized: the US Dollar is unrestricted legal tender in parallel with the Panamanian Balboa (PAB) at an immovable 1:1 exchange rate, and the Balboa circulates only as fractional coinage. There are no exchange controls, no capital-account or current-account restrictions, no prior-authorization regimes, no conversion obligations, and no quantitative limits on any cross-border transfer. Capital contributions, digital-marketplace revenue settlements, royalty licencing payments, dividend distributions, intra-group loan repayments, and sale-of-business proceeds are freely convertible and transferable in either direction. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders faces no FX hurdle and no special tax clearance; the only legal limitations are (i) the standard Panamanian dividend withholding rules applicable strictly to profits derived from Panama-source activities (foreign-source income is outside the territorial tax base), and (ii) bank-level documentary gates such as board minutes, fiscal good-standing certificates, and Law No. 23 of 2015 ultimate-beneficial-owner declarations. For a stock-photo and generative-asset licencing entity operating through a Panama S.A., worldwide digital revenue routed to a USD account is fully convertible without central-bank intervention.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation on export proceeds, digital-service receipts, stock-photo royalties, or subscription/AI-asset licencing fees. The treasury may retain 100% of proceeds in USD or any other currency, disburse them abroad immediately, and maintain offshore balances without any central-bank reporting. The only reporting duties are standard AML thresholds (cash transactions at or above USD 10,000 and suspicious-transaction reports to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero), which are unrelated to FX surrender.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High as an ancillary payment gateway; Low as a primary treasury host. Panama law does not recognise the EU/UK electronic-money-institution (EMI) licence category: any issuance of electronic money callable at par in Panama requires a licence or authorisation from the SBP, and offshore EMIs cannot lawfully provide regulated e-money services to the public inside Panama or hold the Panama S.A.'s principal settlement balances. The legally viable blueprint is to use licensed cross-border PSPs and EMIs (Stripe, PayPal, Wise Platform, Payoneer) strictly as collection forwarders that aggregate worldwide card/alternative-payment-method transactions in the United States or EU and wire net USD proceeds into the Panama operating account at a tier-1 local bank via SWIFT. This structure is compliant because the EMI performs payment facilitation in its own jurisdiction and never acts as a Panamanian bank. Banks will treat PSP-cleared flows as low-risk where a clean funds trail connects the PSP payout report to the Panama account; however, attempting to use an unlicensed EMI as the sole treasury host will trigger enhanced due diligence and likely account refusal.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical verification is the prevailing rule for a newly incorporated, non-resident-owned S.A. SBP risk-based KYC standards require the bank to positively identify the signatories and ultimate beneficial owners, and tier-1 banks will demand an in-person interview of at least one authorised natural-person signatory (the legal representative or an appointed alternate principal) at a Panamanian branch. Pure remote account opening is permitted only on a case-by-case basis for low-risk clients and, even then, only with (i) an apostilled notarised power of attorney, (ii) an SBP-compliant video-identification procedure, and (iii) confirmation of corporate existence from the Public Registry. In practical terms, most tier-1 banks allow the first signer to appear physically while the other directors and UBOs join by video; fully digital onboarding without any physical appearance remains exceptional for an entity whose sole economic activity is cross-border digital media. The resident agent (registered agent) cannot open the account on the company's behalf unless granted an express power of attorney signed before a Panamanian notary and accepted by the bank's compliance unit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or beneficial-owner nexus in FATF grey-listed, sanctioned, or tax-haven-perimeter jurisdictions, or an opaque trust chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed Law No. 23 of 2015 ultimate-beneficial-owner declaration certified by the registered agent; full corporate chain chart from the Public Registry; apostilled passports and recent utility bills for all natural-person UBOs; source-of-funds letter describing the stock-photo and AI-generative-asset monetisation model; sanctions screening results (OFAC, EU, UN); and a sworn statement by the UBOs waiving bearer-share, nominee-trust, or cascade-holding ambiguities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee officers, historical bearer shares pre-2015 reform, or control ambiguity in the S.A. bylaws
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the public deed (escritura pública) and current bylaws showing immobilised shares; Public Registry certification that no bearer-share certificates remain outstanding; express voting trust deeds where professional nominee directors are used; director and officer appointment minutes with legalised signatures; and a substance narrative proving that the Panama entity exercises effective management over the marketplace and licencing operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or high-risk source of funds for AI-generated digital-asset revenue, including layered PSP settlements from Stripe and PayPal and volatile marketplace payout activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month PSP payout statements in the corporate name; platform analytics and revenue reports; executed content-licencing and marketplace terms-of-service contracts; a compliance-prepared payment-flow schematic showing gateway-to-account settlement; CPA-reviewed management accounts; and a written explanation reconciling each batch settlement against the ISIC 7420 digital-revenue ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP status of ultimate shareholders or politically exposed counterparties on the content-licencing side
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP declarations with appointing-organisation confirmation letters; enhanced-due-diligence file containing beneficial-ownership evidence, professional references, primary-bank reference letters from the UBOs, sanctions-screening results, and a statement of independence demonstrating no reputational exposure to the Panamanian financial system.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared territorial business model (Panama S.A. earning worldwide royalty income) and documentation showing only a Delaware or low-tax flag-management entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organisation chart proving the Panama S.A. is the revenue-contracting and royalty-owning entity; executed IP licencing agreements in the Panama name; seller-of-record designations from Stripe and PayPal; the ISIC 7420 business plan; and intercompany service agreements demonstrating substantive functions, assets, and risks located in Panama rather than a pure letterbox structure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital flows are USD-native and route through standard correspondent banking networks: (1) shareholder capital contributions are transmitted via SWIFT MT103 (or MT203 for multi-batch funding) from the parent or subscriber bank to the Panama S.A.'s USD operating account, with the Remittance Information narrative stating 'Aporte de capital / capital contribution' and referencing the capital-increase deed and RUC tax-identification number; (2) the receiving bank verifies the funds against an apostilled copy of the public deed of capital increase, the updated share registry, the shareholders' resolution, and registered-agent certification from the Public Registry; (3) Panama has no central-bank numeric purpose codes, so the narrative field constitutes the primary compliance classification and must be consistent with the corporate treasury documentation to prevent reclassification as a loan, royalty, or service fee; (4) for digital-marketplace receipts from Stripe and PayPal, funds settle from the PSP's USD accounts at US clearing institutions via ACH, Fedwire, or SWIFT and are credited to the Panama operating account, then matched against the platform's payout report to evidence the underlying transactions; (5) banks will refresh source-of-funds and UBO declarations before booking any large one-off capital injection, and legal counsel's letter confirming the payer's authority is generally required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury disbursements use five clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for individual supplier, contractor, licensor, and content-creator payments, executed over the correspondent network with New York CHIPS/Fedwire clearing banks as intermediaries; (ii) SWIFT MT202 COV for interbank treasury sweeps, parent dividends, and beneficiary-bank funding where cover payments are mandated; (iii) commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 (irrevocable, confirmed or unconfirmed) for documentary trade transactions, available through the trade desks of Banistmo and BAC for any physical or service-side supply chain, although digital stock-photo licencing is normally settled by invoice plus wire; (iv) PSP mass-payout engines (PayPal Mass Payout and Stripe Payouts) for disbursements to global content creators, where the PSP performs FX conversion and local-rail delivery outside Panama; and (v) the Panama local ACH system managed by the banking association for domestic B2B payments and Panamanian payroll. Because the corporate account is USD-denominated and Panama has no domestic FX market, outbound USD disbursements remain on the international correspondent clearing system without central-bank approval; non-USD beneficiary payments are converted by the bank's international desk at prevailing interbank rates, with no withholding tax on foreign-source profit remittance under the territorial tax system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forwards with international banking counterparties (Banistmo/Bancolombia international desks, Scotiabank Global FX) to fix EUR, GBP, or other conversion rates on content-licencing royalties and subscription receivables; no Balboa/USD forward market exists because the PAB is rigidly pegged at 1:1 to USD

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing Latin American currencies (COP, MXN, BRL) where regional marketplace receivables create documented exposure, transacted through parent-bank offices or international desks because local NDF market depth inside Panama is negligible

Cross-currency swaps governed by an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex, converting EUR/GBP platform revenue into synthetic USD, permissible under Panamanian banking law as ordinary off-balance-sheet derivatives for corporate clients with verified underlying exposure

European-style OTC FX options for contingency hedging on large one-off licencing or asset-sale deals, permissible when supported by a realistic underlying exposure, board authorisation minutes, and a compliant derivatives-eligibility assessment by the SBP-regulated counterparty bank

Strategic unhedged USD position as the default treasury policy, given that the entity's functional currency is USD and Panama's dollarised legal tender system eliminates domestic translation and convertibility risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Franchise Tax (Tasa Única / Anualidad)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá / Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June; first-year fee is paid at incorporation; subsequent renewals are due by 30 June of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment is subject to statutory penalty and interest; after three consecutive years of non-payment, the Public Registry may administratively strike off or dissolve the S.A., causing loss of good standing; the resident agent may also resign.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Sworn Confirmation (Declaración de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - Registro de Beneficiarios Finales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 July, or as fixed by DGI resolution; any share transfer or change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be updated within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or to maintain accurate UBO data triggers administrative fines under the AML/beneficial-owner regime, suspension of registration of corporate acts in the Public Registry, and possible loss of good standing; wilful false filings may be criminally sanctioned.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Panama Law 32 of 1927 imposes no automatic statutory audit on a private S.A. solely by reason of turnover, assets, or employees for a non-resident stock-photo platform. Mandatory audit is triggered only where (i) the articles/bylaws/shareholders' agreement require it, (ii) a court orders it, (iii) an independent audit is required by a regulated Panamanian supervisor (banking, securities, insurance, gaming, trust), or (iv) an auditor is appointed by a lender/investor or for consolidation purposes. A non-regulated S.A. may maintain unaudited management accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panamanian generally accepted accounting principles are aligned with International Financial Reporting Standards as issued by the IASB; private SMEs may use the IFRS for SMEs framework. Entities that conduct activities in Panama must keep DGI-compliant accounting records; records must be retained for at least 7 years and be made available in Spanish or with Spanish translation when required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 70 of 2017 and DGI beneficial-owner rules, the S.A. must maintain a resident agent and file an annual sworn confirmation in the DGI beneficial-owner registry. The confirmation identifies each ultimate beneficial owner and the ownership or control percentage. In addition, a transfer of shares is effective against the corporation only when recorded in the Register of Members; the UBO registry and KYC file must be updated within 30 days of the transfer. The resident agent obtains KYC documents (passport, proof of residence, source of funds, corporate chain) and files through the DGI electronic portal.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Officers (Registro de Directores)
Minute Book of shareholders' and directors' meetings (Libro de Actas)
Beneficial Ownership File / UBO Register maintained with the resident agent

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - USD 750 per annum, depending on the Panamanian law firm or registered agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 4,000 per annum for an independent review or audit of a small non-resident S.A.; regulated-entity full audits typically USD 6,000 and up

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (top marginal rate on net Panama-source taxable income exceeding USD 1,500,000; 10% on the first USD 50,000; 15% on the band from USD 50,001 to USD 1,500,000)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies a territorial-source system: ISR (Impuesto sobre la Renta) attaches only to Panama-source profits. Stock-photography licensing, AI-generated visual-asset sales, API licensing and platform distributions executed abroad - with contracts, management, servers and payment collection outside Panama - fall outside the Panamanian tax base, producing an effective 0% rate on demonstrably foreign-source income. No statutory tax holiday applies to a standard Sociedad Anónima in ISIC 7420 activity; the preferential effective rate is achieved exclusively through territorial-source exemption, supported by substance documentation and a timely-filed return.
